note: Excerpt of the local Windows System event log around the R1w run, extracted after the run on 2026-09-30 with Get-WinEvent: LogName System, from 2026-09-29 20:00 to the extraction time, all Kernel-Power events and Power-Troubleshooter 1 (none of the latter in the window). 506 is the system entering modern standby, 507 leaving it, 566 a change of the system session's state. The last events before the run are the exit from modern standby and a change of the system session's state (7 to 9), both at 22:00:24.417 on 2026-09-29; there is none after them up to the extraction time, so none during the run. The log alone does not show when the process could run. Each event's 'message' is the first line of its text, as in R1v's excerpt. Added on 2026-10-01, while the write-up was checked before commit: in run_timing, the launch time, the log file's and the fields file's times, the range by which the process outlasts the timer, and the tighter timer start (the record's and the manifest's file times, and the solves' clock times, date from 30 September; the record's was then rounded to the millisecond); and the power-source changes in power_source.
extracted_with: Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='System'; StartTime='2026-09-29 20:00'; EndTime=<now>}, filtered to provider Microsoft-Windows-Kernel-Power, and Microsoft-Windows-Power-Troubleshooter id 1

run_timing.launched_note: the session's own record: the shell call that started the pipeline 'python -u scripts/zhao2d_r1w_pool_screen.py | grep | tee results/zhao2d_r1w.log' is stamped 01:36:36.359 and its acknowledgement 01:36:36.405; none of the script's outputs holds it (copied here on 2026-10-01)
